items.title: Isotropic eddy viscosity and unresolved energy model
items.design_state: Step 1 draft authored; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Adopted three-dimensional isotropic stress-form closure for smooth, periodic, constant-density incompressible Newtonian large-eddy models using the stated positive convolution filter. The nonnegative specific unresolved energy and kinematic eddy-viscosity fields are model inputs; no coefficient law, empirical validation, universal applicability, or equality with the exact filtered covariance is asserted.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice for the normalized periodic torus convention. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open time interval, let $L>0$ m, and let $\mathbb T_L^3=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^3$ have volume measure $dx$ on a period cell and normalized measure $d\mu_L=L^{-3}dx$. Coordinates $x,r,L,\ell$ are measured in metres and time $t$ in seconds. All spacetime fields below use the ordered domain $\mathbb T_L^3\times I$ and evaluation $(x,t)$; for a time-indexed spatial field $q$, write $q(x,t):=(q(t))(x)$. Let $K:\mathbb R^3\to[0,\infty)$ be smooth, dimensionless, supported in a compact subset of $B_1(0)$, and satisfy $\int_{\mathbb R^3}K(s)\,ds=1$. For $0<\ell<L/2$, define

$$G_\ell(r)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z^3}\ell^{-3}K\!\left(\frac{r+Ln}{\ell}\right),\qquad \overline q_\ell(x,t)=\int_{\mathbb T_L^3}G_\ell(r)q(x-r,t)\,dr.$$

The kernel $G_\ell$ has units m$^{-3}$ and filtering preserves the units of $q$.

The physical base model is the smooth, unforced, constant-density incompressible Newtonian branch: $\rho_0>0$ kg m$^{-3}$ and dynamic viscosity $\mu\ge0$ Pa s are constant, $u\in C^1(I;C^\infty(\mathbb T_L^3;\mathbb R^3))$ is periodic with $\nabla\cdot u=0$ and velocity units m s$^{-1}$, and the pressure multiplier is a periodic scalar field $p_{\rm dyn}\in C^1(\mathbb T_L^3\times I;\mathbb R)$ in Pa. Let $I_3$ be the $3\times3$ identity matrix and set $D(u)=(\nabla u+(\nabla u)^T)/2$; the dynamic Cauchy stress is $\sigma=-p_{\rm dyn}I_3+2\mu D(u)$, and $\nu=\mu/\rho_0$ m$^2$ s$^{-1}$. The pressure per unit mass in the filtered equation is the filtered scalar field $\pi_\ell=\overline{p_{\rm dyn}}_\ell/\rho_0\in C^1(\mathbb T_L^3\times I;\mathbb R)$ in m$^2$ s$^{-2}$, where $\overline{p_{\rm dyn}}_\ell(x,t)=\int_{\mathbb T_L^3}G_\ell(r)p_{\rm dyn}(x-r,t)\,dr$, and $\nabla\pi_\ell$ denotes its spatial gradient. The isotropic modeled term $2kI_3/3$ remains in $\tau_\ell^{\rm model}$ below; it is not absorbed into $\pi_\ell$.

For the filtered velocity $\overline u_\ell$, define its rate-of-strain tensor by

$$D_\ell=\frac12\left(\nabla\overline u_\ell+(\nabla\overline u_\ell)^T\right),\qquad (\nabla\overline u_\ell)_{ij}=\partial_j\overline u_{\ell,i}.$$

The matrix $D_\ell$ has units s$^{-1}$. Use the Frobenius contraction $A:B=\sum_{i,j=1}^3A_{ij}B_{ij}$ for real $3\times3$ matrices.

Adopt the following large-eddy simulation (LES) stress-form closure. A closure here means a specified modeled stress substituted for the exact filtered covariance in the resolved momentum equation. Let $k,\nu_t\in C^1(\mathbb T_L^3\times I;[0,\infty))$ be prescribed model fields, where $k$ represents specific unresolved kinetic energy in m$^2$ s$^{-2}$ and $\nu_t$ is kinematic eddy viscosity in m$^2$ s$^{-1}$. The modeled specific subfilter stress and its modeled transfer are

$$\tau_{\ell}^{\rm model}=\frac{2k}{3}I_3-2\nu_tD_\ell,\qquad \Pi_{\ell}^{\rm model}=-\tau_{\ell}^{\rm model}:\nabla\overline u_\ell.$$

The closed filtered momentum equation uses the sign convention

$$\partial_t\overline u_\ell+\nabla\cdot(\overline u_\ell\otimes\overline u_\ell)+\nabla\pi_\ell=\nu\Delta\overline u_\ell-\nabla\cdot\tau_{\ell}^{\rm model},\qquad \nabla\cdot\overline u_\ell=0.$$

Both terms in $\tau_{\ell}^{\rm model}$ have units m$^2$ s$^{-2}$, and $\Pi_{\ell}^{\rm model}$ has units m$^2$ s$^{-3}$. This is an adopted constitutive form, not a derivation of a physical law: $k$ and $\nu_t$ must be supplied as model inputs or by separate model equations. The prescription does not assert that $\tau_{\ell}^{\rm model}$ equals the exact covariance $\overline{u\otimes u}_\ell-\overline u_\ell\otimes\overline u_\ell$, that the modeled tensor is positive semidefinite, or that the closure is empirically adequate in every flow regime. No absence of backscatter for the exact filtered stress is asserted.

items.title: Resolved dissipation of adopted eddy viscosity
items.design_state: Step 1 draft authored; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Pointwise resolved stress-transfer identity for the adopted smooth, periodic, three-dimensional incompressible Newtonian closure. The nonnegative result concerns only the modeled eddy-viscosity stress. It does not assert a sign for the exact filtered covariance, model accuracy, a solution-existence result, or universal absence of backscatter.

items.title: Adopted simple shear production
items.design_state: Step 1 draft authored; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Pointwise simple-shear state of the adopted three-dimensional LES closure. This is an exact model calculation, not a measured flow or a solution- existence claim.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice for the normalized periodic-torus convention. Let $I\subset\mathbb R$ be an open time interval measured in seconds, $L>0$ m, $0<\ell<L/2$, and $\mathbb T_L^3=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^3$. All spacetime fields below use the ordered domain $\mathbb T_L^3\times I$ and evaluation $(x,t)$; for a time-indexed spatial field $q$, write $q(x,t):=(q(t))(x)$. Let $u\in C^1(I;C^\infty(\mathbb T_L^3;\mathbb R^3))$ be a periodic divergence-free velocity field measured in m s$^{-1}$. Let $K:\mathbb R^3\to[0,\infty)$ be smooth, dimensionless, supported in a compact subset of $B_1(0)$, and satisfy $\int_{\mathbb R^3}K(s)\,ds=1$. Define

$$G_\ell(r)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z^3}\ell^{-3}K\!\left(\frac{r+Ln}{\ell}\right),\qquad \overline u_\ell(x,t)=\int_{\mathbb T_L^3}G_\ell(r)u(x-r,t)\,dr,$$

where $dx$ is volume measure on a period cell. Thus $\overline u_\ell:\mathbb T_L^3\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ is the resolved velocity field, with position in metres and velocity in m s$^{-1}$. The periodic filter commutes with spatial derivatives, so $\overline u_\ell$ is divergence-free. Let $k,\nu_t\in C^1(\mathbb T_L^3\times I;[0,\infty))$ be prescribed specific unresolved kinetic-energy and kinematic eddy-viscosity fields, measured in m$^2$ s$^{-2}$ and m$^2$ s$^{-1}$, respectively. Use $(\nabla\overline u_\ell)_{ij}=\partial_j\overline u_{\ell,i}$, let $I_3$ be the $3\times3$ identity matrix, and define $A:B=\sum_{i,j=1}^3A_{ij}B_{ij}$ and $|A|_F^2=A:A$ for real $3\times3$ matrices. Define

$$D_\ell=\frac12\left(\nabla\overline u_\ell+(\nabla\overline u_\ell)^T\right).$$

For the adopted closure, define the modeled specific stress and transfer by $\tau_{\ell}^{\rm model}=2kI_3/3-2\nu_tD_\ell$ and $\Pi_{\ell}^{\rm model}=-\tau_{\ell}^{\rm model}:\nabla\overline u_\ell$. At a point $(x_0,t_0)\in\mathbb T_L^3\times I$, suppose the velocity gradient is

$$\nabla\overline u_\ell(x_0,t_0)=\begin{pmatrix}0&S&0\\0&0&0\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix},$$

where $S\in\mathbb R$ is the local shear rate in s$^{-1}$. Put $k_0=k(x_0,t_0)$ and $\nu_0=\nu_t(x_0,t_0)$. Then the modeled transfer at $(x_0,t_0)$ is $\nu_0S^2$ m$^2$ s$^{-3}$. This is a pointwise calculation in the adopted closure model; it asserts no measured value, finite-time evolution, or sign for exact filtered transfer.
